manuscript_claim: Full-channel classifiers achieve above-chance subject-independent gesture recognition under strict participant-level LOSO evaluation.
Explainability-derived channel rankings show significant cross-subject stability.
supporting_result: Mean Spearman rank correlation rho = 0.84 across outer fold rankings
statistical_test: Spearman rank correlation and Kendall tau

manuscript_claim: A reduced channel configuration exists that is statistically non-inferior to the full array under a prespecified Macro-F1 margin delta = 0.02.
supporting_result: k* = 6 channels achieves Macro-F1 = 0.841 with LCB_95(Delta) > -0.02

manuscript_claim: Explainability-guided channel selection performs significantly better than random selection and competitively with conventional baselines.
supporting_result: SHAP selection outperforms random selection (p < 0.001) and geometry spread across all k
statistical_test: Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Holm correction

manuscript_claim: Channel importance shows measurable stability across recording sessions.
The sparse-channel methodology reproduces qualitatively on NinaPro DB5 even though hardware and acquisition differ.
supporting_result: Non-inferior performance retained using ~37% channels (k=6/16) on DB5
